SECOND STORYLINE, a genuinely NEW and more severe rendering defect discovered today: on both /en/explore (explore-map.tsx) and /en/destination/betla (destination-map.tsx, this session's non-cinematic Leaflet control), the Leaflet map's internal tile pane AND marker pane render their content several THOUSAND pixels outside the actual visible container bounds (e.g. on /explore, a 1280x600px container measured markers at boundingClientRect.top=5482 -- ~4900px below the container's own bottom edge; identical pattern on betla, 0/4 markers and 0/84 tiles falling inside the container rect). This is NOT the same failure as yesterday's CARTO 'API KEY REQUIRED' watermark (NEW-2026-08-31-001, independently reconfirmed STILL OPEN today via direct tile fetch -- byte-identical 7907-byte watermarked PNG) -- it is a distinct, compounding defect: today the map area is not merely watermarked, it is 100% blank because NONE of the 519 (explore) or 4 (betla) markers, and NONE of the 30-84 loaded tiles, fall inside the visible viewport at all, regardless of tile content. Reproduced 3 independent ways to rule out a testing-harness artifact: (a) JS scrollIntoView, (b) real mouse-wheel scroll via computer:scroll, (c) DOM-based scroll_to on a fresh tab at a clean 1430px desktop viewport with no prior navigation/resize history -- all three show the same thousands-of-pixels marker/tile offset. Toggling Grid->Map->Grid->Map again did not self-heal it. window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')) did not self-heal it either (Leaflet needs an explicit map.invalidateSize() call, which nothing in the page appears to trigger). This reads as a container-resized-after-Leaflet-init desync (the classic Leaflet gotcha when the map's container position/size changes post-mount without invalidateSize() being called), affecting BOTH Leaflet-consuming surfaces. Root cause NOT pinned to today's 2 shipped commits -- neither explore-map.tsx nor destination-map.tsx was touched in either diff, and the shared file both commits DID touch (nav.tsx) only changed a hamburger-button className. Onset date unknown: no prior QA session ever checked marker/tile getBoundingClientRect() against the container's own rect (only counted DOM elements), so this could have been broken before today too -- flagging as newly-DISCOVERED today via an improved methodology, not asserting a regression start date. new_findings_today.title: Leaflet map tiles AND markers render several thousand pixels outside their own container's visible bounds -- both /en/explore and destination pages (e.g. betla) show a 100% blank map area, a distinct and more severe defect than yesterday's CARTO-watermark issue
new_findings_today.detail: While re-verifying yesterday's CARTO watermark finding (NEW-2026-08-31-001, confirmed STILL OPEN), this session went a step further and compared every rendered marker's and tile's getBoundingClientRect() against the .leaflet-container's own boundingClientRect, on both Leaflet-consuming surfaces. On /en/explore's Map view (1280x600px container, 519 markers per the UI's own '519 markers - colored by score' label), 0 of 519 markers and 0 of 84 loaded tiles fall inside the container's visible rect -- a sample marker measured at boundingClientRect.top=5482, roughly 4900px below the container's own bottom edge (bottom=1173). On /en/destination/betla (this session's out-of-sample non-cinematic Leaflet control), the identical pattern reproduces: 0 of 4 markers and 0 of tiles measured fall inside the container, with markers found at y-offsets thousands of pixels away from the container's actual position (which itself moves correctly as the page scrolls -- only the INTERNAL pane content is desynced). All tiles report .complete=true and naturalWidth=256 (they load successfully, this is not a network failure) and all markers have real SVG path elements with fill/opacity set (they are not hidden via CSS) -- the panes simply render their content at pixel coordinates that do not correspond to the container's current position/size. This produces a visually blank, uniform dark-navy rectangle with no discernible tiles, markers, or even the CARTO watermark text (since the watermarked tile, if present, is also off-canvas). Reproduced 3 independent ways specifically to rule out a testing-harness artifact: JS scrollIntoView, a real mouse-wheel scroll via the computer tool, and a DOM-based scroll_to -- all 3 on fresh tabs, one at a ~596px mobile-emulated viewport and one at a clean 1430px desktop viewport with no prior resize/navigation history. Toggling the explore page's Grid->Map->Grid->Map control again did not self-correct it, and manually dispatching a window 'resize' event did not either -- consistent with the classic Leaflet gotcha where a map's internal pixel origin is computed once at L.map() initialization and never resynced via map.invalidateSize() if the container's position or size changes afterward (e.g. due to images, fonts, or banner content above it finishing their layout shift after the lazy-mounted map has already initialized).
new_findings_today.evidence: JS getBoundingClientRect() comparisons captured live during the session: explore map container {x:71,y:573.6,width:1280,height:600} vs sample marker {x:1085,y:5482.6} (0/519 markers, 0/84 tiles inside bounds); betla map container measured at multiple scroll positions (e.g. {y:-2499.8, height:384}) vs sample marker {y:5899.2} (0/4 markers inside bounds, offset from container position by ~8400px). Tile elements confirmed .complete=true, naturalWidth=256, class 'leaflet-tile-loaded' -- ruling out a load failure. Screenshots taken at each stage (mobile and desktop viewports, before and after scroll) all show a uniform blank dark-navy map area with no visible tiles or markers.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Have engineering call map.invalidateSize() (or re-render the map on a ResizeObserver bound to the container) after the destination page's/explore page's above-the-fold content finishes its layout shift, and specifically after any lazy-mount-on-scroll-into-view trigger fires -- the current mount timing appears to capture a stale size/position. Since this compounds the already-open CARTO watermark issue (NEW-2026-08-31-001) into a fully non-functional map feature (0% visible content, not just wrong-looking content), and /explore is top-nav-accessible, this should be treated as at least as urgent as that item. Worth adding a getBoundingClientRect()-vs-container check to Section K's standing methodology going forward, since prior sessions' element-count-only checks would not have caught this.
